Our work spans from developing foundational meta-science methods to high-resolution mapping of the human exposome and personal health trajectories.

## Foundational Meta-Science & Robustness

**[Vibration of Effects in Observational Research](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclinepi.2015.03.029)** *Patel et al., J Clin Epidemiol, 2015* Introduced the "Vibration of Effects" (VoE) framework to quantify how statistical choices change study outcomes. This paper underpins our group's focus on reproducible research.  
[Altmetric: 1706](https://scienceadvances.altmetric.com/details/164234372)

**[Systematically Assessing Drivers of Inconsistency in Metagenomics](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3001556)** *Tierney et al., PLoS Biology, 2022* We re-analyzed 581 microbiome–disease associations to demonstrate how analytic choices drive conflicting results, providing a template for robust discovery in high-dimensional data.

---

## Mapping the Global Exposome-Phenome

**[An Atlas of Genetic and Environmental Contributions to 560 Phenotypes](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-018-0313-7)** *Lakhani et al., Nature Genetics, 2019* By repurposing U.S. insurance claims, we created a "shared exposome atlas" showing that non-genetic factors are significant drivers of most common diseases.  
[Altmetric: 874](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41588-018-0313-7/metrics)

**[The Landscape of Genetic Content in the Human Microbiome](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chom.2019.07.008)** *Tierney et al., Cell Host & Microbe, 2019* Moved beyond species-level taxonomy to a gene-centric view of the microbiome, treating microbial genes as a functional 'omics layer for precision medicine.

**[An Atlas of Exposome-Phenome Associations](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-026-0000-0)** *Patel et al., Nature Medicine, 2026 (In Press)* A decade of research synthesized into a single characterization of the "architecture" of how the environment relates to the clinical phenome, serving as a blueprint for the **NEXUS** consortium.

---

## Precision Prevention & Predictive Modeling

**[Polyexposure Scores in Risk Prediction of Type 2 Diabetes](https://doi.org/10.2337/dc20-2134)** *He et al., Diabetes Care, 2021* Formalized "polyexposure risk scores" as a clinical counterpart to genetics, quantifying how much incremental information the exposome adds to diabetes prediction.

**[Using Deep Learning to Predict Abdominal Age from MRI](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29615-9)** *Le Goallec et al., Nature Communications, 2022* Developed AI to predict "organ-specific age," linking structural changes in the liver and pancreas to metabolic and cardiometabolic risk.

**[Timing and Consistency of Physical Activity](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00125-023-05991-w)** *Tian et al., Diabetologia, 2023* Proved that high-resolution behavioral timing (accelerometry) is a critical, modifiable risk factor for diabetes, informing precision lifestyle guidance.  
[Altmetric: 630](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00125-023-05991-w)

---

## Future Directions: From Observation to Translation

**[Personalized Glucose Trajectories (SSM-CGM)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04386)** *Isaac et al., arXiv, 2025 (NeurIPS Workshop)* A "state-space" machine learning model that allows individuals to run "what-if" simulations on how their behavior affects blood sugar in real-time.

**[Plasma Proteomics & Lifestyle Exposome](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.05.07.25327178v1)** *Isaac et al., medRxiv, 2025* Developed the Human Exposomic Architecture of the Proteome (HEAP) to show how lifestyle modifications target the same biological pathways as modern therapeutics.

**[Exposome vs. Biomarkers in Alzheimer’s Prognosis](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.11.19.25340533)** *Ellis et al., medRxiv, 2025* A head-to-head comparison proving that low-cost, scalable assessments of modifiable risk are as effective as invasive biomarkers for AD screening in asymptomatic populations.
